about.body: Daniel and Rosa Hale planted their first vines on a steep, rocky ridge above St. Helena in 1998, when everyone told them it was too steep to farm. Today their daughter Maya makes the wines. The whole family still picks at harvest.

The vineyards sit on a hillside ridge above St. Helena in Napa Valley. The family farms 40 acres organically and dry farms every block, with no irrigation, so the roots go deep. Every cluster is picked by hand in the cool early morning.
The wines are made in a stone winery built into the hillside in 2004. Its barrel cave stays cool all year. The winery makes about 3,000 cases a year.

The tasting room sits on the terrace above the vines, with views across the valley to the Mayacamas. Choose the Estate tasting of five wines on the terrace, or the 90-minute Vineyard and cellar walk that ends with a barrel tasting. Tastings are by reservation.
